hook.text: Before 1982, diabetics injected pig or cow insulin — it sometimes caused allergic reactions. Then came Humulin.

buildup.text: Genentech inserted the human insulin gene into E. coli bacteria — the microbes became tiny insulin factories.

discovery.text: Humulin was the first recombinant drug approved by the FDA — identical to human insulin, made by bacteria.

twist.text: Modern insulin analogs are engineered beyond human — lispro acts faster, glargine lasts longer. Better than nature.

climax.text: Over 100 million people depend on recombinant insulin — the first biopharmaceutical saved an entire industry.

punchline.text: Bacteria make human insulin — biotech's first drug, still saving lives.

quiz.question: What made Humulin historically significant?
options: It was the first insulin that could be taken orally
It was the first recombinant DNA drug approved by the FDA
It was extracted from a new animal source
